passages.text: BRAIN, in anatomy, the soft mass contained within the skull, divided into the cerebrum, or brain properly so called, and the cerebellum, or little brain, placed behind and below it.
It consists of two substances: an outer, of an ash colour, called the cortical; and an inner, white, called the medullary.
The brain is the seat of sensation and the organ of the mind; for when it is injured, sense and motion are destroyed or disordered.
The nerves arise from the brain and spinal marrow, and convey to it the impressions of objects, and from it the commands of the will.
Des Cartes placed the seat of the soul in the pineal gland; but this opinion has no foundation.
The cerebellum is thought by some to preside over the vital motions, as the beating of the heart and breathing, which go on without our will.
The brain of man is larger, in proportion to his body, than that of any other animal.
The human brain is the central organ of the nervous system. Its main parts are the cerebrum, the brainstem and the cerebellum, which lies at the back, below the cerebrum.
The outer layer of the cerebrum, the cerebral cortex, is made of grey matter; beneath it lies white matter, made of nerve fibres.
The brain controls most activities of the body, processing information from the senses and producing thought, memory and voluntary movement.
Nerves carry signals from the senses to the brain and spinal cord, and from them to the muscles.
The pineal gland produces the hormone melatonin, which helps regulate sleep. Rene Descartes believed it was the seat of the soul.
The cerebellum coordinates movement and balance. Breathing and heart rate are controlled by the brainstem.
Relative to body size the human brain is unusually large, though some small animals have a higher ratio of brain weight to body weight.
The brain contains about 86 billion neurons, which communicate by electrical and chemical signals.

reasons: The 1797 headword BRAIN matches the Wikipedia article on the human brain.
Rare terms appear in both: cerebrum, cerebellum, cortical, pineal gland, Descartes.
Brain (all animals) scores on the headword but is less specific than Human brain.

suggestedQuestions: Did the 1797 entry agree with Descartes about the pineal gland?
What did the 1797 entry think the cerebellum does?

Did the 1797 entry agree with Descartes.answer: No. It says Descartes placed the soul in the pineal gland, but that the opinion has no foundation [B5]. Wikipedia says the gland produces melatonin, which helps regulate sleep [W5].

What did the 1797 entry think the cerebe.answer: Some thought it governed the vital motions, such as the heartbeat and breathing [B6]. Wikipedia says the cerebellum coordinates movement and balance, and that breathing and heart rate are controlled by the brainstem [W6].
